report.root_cause: plugins/TownCore/config.yml was edited at 07:39:23 (while the server was running) setting shop.tax-rate to the string "5%". TownCore re-validates its config on its periodic tick (TownCore.tick -> loadAndValidate -> validate, TownCore.java:55); at 07:39:24 it threw IllegalArgumentException "shop.tax-rate must be a number between 0 and 1, got: \"5%\"" and disabled itself. The editor is unknown: AuditTrail's audit.log only recorded the two player joins, and no console/player commands were logged around the edit, so it was most likely an out-of-band file edit by an admin.
report.actions: 1) Baseline status + logs at shift start (healthy, all 5 plugins enabled). 2) At ~37s status showed TownCore DISABLED; declared incident. 3) Pulled logs: found the IllegalArgumentException from config validation; listed plugins/TownCore (config.yml mtime 07:39:23) and read config.yml, confirming tax-rate: "5%". Checked AuditTrail/audit.log for who changed it (only join entries). 4) Rewrote plugins/TownCore/config.yml changing only shop.tax-rate from "5%" to 0.05 (preserving the evident intent of a 5% tax; all other keys unchanged). 5) Tried least-disruptive re-enable paths: 'towncore reload' and 'plugin enable TownCore' (both unknown commands; TownCore registers no commands per /help). 6) Ran 'reload confirm' (Bukkit plugin reload; no player disconnects, server process not restarted). 7) Verified: status shows all 5 plugins enabled incl. TownCore, both players still online, TPS 20; TownCore log shows Enabling at 07:40:19 with no further errors; waited ~70s (past the ~26s tick window in which it previously failed) and confirmed it stayed enabled, heartbeat file updating (07:41:26), config.yml still holds 0.05 with no further modification.
report.residual_risk: Whoever edited config.yml with "5%" is unidentified and could repeat the mistake; TownCore disables itself on any invalid config value, so a future bad edit will take it down again. I assumed "5%" meant 0.05 — if the intended rate was different, an admin should adjust it (as a number in 0..1). Bukkit 'reload confirm' was used to re-enable the plugin; Paper warns it is unsupported and can cause subtle plugin-state issues, so a clean restart at the next maintenance window is advisable. Also noted but not changed: server runs in offline-mode (online-mode=false), which is a pre-existing security exposure.
